insights.headline: Gold retests $4,200 as softer dollar and yields fuel Friday rebound; festive buying picks up in India
insights.summary: Spot gold climbed 1.5% to about $4,194 on Friday, testing the $4,200 level as a softer US dollar, retreating Treasury yields and bargain buying reversed a midweek selloff, with silver up 2.77% near $60.70. In India, retailers report gold buying picking up after the price correction, with shoppers prioritising affordability ahead of the festival season. Policy stays in focus: India has not extended the 3% IGST exemption on bullion imports by banks, and the RBI tightened forex derivative rules; September CPI on October 14 is the next key test for the Fed's rate path.
points: Spot gold rose 1.5% to ~$4,194 on Friday, testing $4,200 as dollar softness, easing Treasury yields and bargain buying reversed the midweek selloff.
Silver gained 2.77% to ~$60.70 on Friday alongside gold; MCX December silver rose 1.64% to Rs 2.24 lakh/kg.
Gold buying is picking up after the price correction but shoppers prioritise affordability, retailers say; PN Gadgil's Q2 revenue rose 22.4% on festive demand.
India has not extended the 3% IGST exemption on gold, silver and platinum imports by banks since April 1, 2026, per the Revenue Secretary.
Traders price a 19% chance of an October Fed hike and 84% for at least one by December; September CPI on October 14 is the next key data point.

trending.title: The $4,200 test
trending.summary: Gold's Friday rebound reversed the midweek selloff as softer yields and a weaker dollar overpowered rate-hike fears; whether it holds above $4,180-$4,200 into next week's CPI will set the tone.

trending.title: Festival demand vs high prices
trending.summary: Indian retailers report footfall recovering after the price correction but wallets staying tight, while jewellers post strong festive-season numbers ahead of Diwali.

trending.title: Policy tightening at the margins
trending.summary: The lapsed IGST exemption for bank bullion imports and tighter RBI forex-derivative rules add friction for Indian market participants.

trending.title: Record ETF demand meets a softer dollar
trending.summary: Gold-backed ETFs added 67.3 tonnes in September to a record 4,256 tonnes, with Q3 inflows of a record $31 billion — investors bought the dip even as prices fell.

items.title: Gold buying picks up after price correction, but shoppers prioritise affordability
items.summary: Indian gold retailers report customer footfall picking up after the price correction from the highs, but shoppers are prioritising affordability and staying within budgets, ET Bureau reports.

items.title: Gold tests $4,200 as weak sentiment offsets sticky inflation expectations
items.summary: Spot gold traded near $4,194.50 an ounce, up 1.5%, in late US trading Friday as a softer dollar, retreating Treasury yields and bargain buying reversed the midweek selloff. Silver traded near $60.70, up 2.77%. Traders priced a 19% chance of an October Fed hike and 84% for at least one by December, with September CPI on October 14 the next key test.

India has not extended the IGST exemption on gold, silver and platinum imports by banks and nominated agencies, and banks have paid 3% IGST since April 1, 2026, Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava confirmed. The government informed the GST Council at its 57th meeting, citing tax parity across import routes. The exemption dated to 2017, when gold imports were tightly canalised.

items.summary: Spot gold rose 1.5% to $4,194.36 on Friday, touching a one-week high and heading for a ~1.3% weekly gain as bargain buying emerged after Wednesday's two-month low. US December futures settled at $4,216.3. Analysts see a floor near $4,000; traders price a 19% chance of an October Fed hike and 84% for at least one by December, with next week's US CPI the catalyst.
items.title: Gold hits one-week high, heads for weekly gain on bargain-hunting

items.summary: Spot gold hit a weekly high of $4,207.48 early Friday before closing just short of $4,200 resistance, Kitco's weekly survey reports. Wall Street analysts are back near a bullish majority while fewer than half of Main Street respondents expect gains next week. Weak US consumer sentiment (46.3) and rising inflation expectations reinforced gold's hedge appeal, with next week's CPI and PPI in focus.
items.title: Wall Street nears bullish majority after gold's late-week rally
Positive ETF Gold flows pushed holdings to a new record in September
items.summary: World Gold Council data shows gold-backed ETFs added 67.3 tonnes in September to a record 4,256 tonnes, with Q3 inflows of 211 tonnes valued at a record US$31 billion despite falling prices. North American funds led September with US$4 billion of inflows, suggesting investors treated the price pullback as a chance to build positions.

MCX December gold futures rose Rs 1,690 (1.13%) to Rs 1.51 lakh/10g on Friday; December silver gained Rs 3,626 (1.64%) to Rs 2.24 lakh/kg, tracking global gains as US yields eased and the dollar weakened, CNBC TV18 reports. A strong 30-year Treasury auction and softer oil after the US postponed a potential Iran strike helped. Gold ETF holdings may be rising for a 12th straight week.

items.summary: The RBI has tightened rupee-linked forex derivative rules: dealers may no longer allow rebooking of cancelled INR contracts, and the threshold for deals without underlying exposure drops from $100m to $5m, including on exchanges. Dealers must take undertakings against double-hedging and keep a 20% cash Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve with the RBI for covered contracts above $2m notional.
items.title: RBI tightens forex derivative rules: What changes for hedging, cancelled trades

items.summary: PN Gadgil Jewellers reported a 22.4% year-on-year rise in Q2 revenue, led by 31.1% retail growth and 25.5% same-store sales growth, crediting strong retail performance and festive demand, CNBC TV18 reports. Raksha Bandhan sales jumped 114% in pieces and 142% in value versus last year. Gold revenue grew 23.5%, diamond 21% and silver 12%. The jeweller has 80 stores, targeting 103 by end-FY27.
items.title: PN Gadgil Jewellers Q2 revenue jumps 22.4% on festive demand

items.summary: India's forex reserves fell $12.95bn to $734.61bn in the week ended October 2, RBI data released Friday showed, per ANI. Foreign currency assets dropped $10.66bn to $604.75bn, while gold reserves declined $2.29bn to $106.41bn. Reserves remain $43.5bn above end-March 2026 levels and $34.6bn higher year-on-year, as the RBI keeps managing rupee volatility.
items.title: India's forex reserves fall $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion in week ended Oct 2
